r to registered at the instance of one Anil Kumar S/o Shri 3.

According to the applicant, has been named as accused, in this case, on the basis of confession, allegedly made by the other co- accused and all the allegations, which have been leveled against him, are stated to be incorrect.
4. According to the applicant, he is a permanent resident of District Kangra and having deep roots in the society.

5. According to him, two cases have already been registered against him, the details have been mentioned in the application, which is reproduced as under:

8. When put to notice, the Police has filed the status report disclosing therein that on 15.05.2023,

complainant-Anil Kumar appeared before the police and got recorded his statement under Section 154 Cr.P.C.
disclosing therein that he is a student and also doing the part-time job in a private TV Channel.

From the last one year, he is residing in a paying guest accommodation at Shyam Nagar,
Dharamshala.

Along with him, 5-6 other .
boys were also residing there.
Accused-Sahil also used to reside with them.
Accused-Sahil developed friendly relations with the complainant and allure the complainant for helping him in the opening of the bank account.
Since, the complainant was in dire need for a bank account, as such, on 20.02.2023, he has handed over the relevant documents to said Sahil.
Sahil took him to the branch of Canara Bank, Kotwali Bazaar where, his bank account was opened.
Thereafter, Sahil obtained the phone number and e-mail ID of the complainant, on the pretext that the same has to be linked with the bank account.
Sahil has assured him that his account will be opened within few days and thereafter, he will get a message, on his mobile phone.
After waiting for sufficient time, when, the complainant did not receive any message, then, he has contacted Sahil.
Sahil assured him that his account will be opened soon.
When, accused-Sahil could not give the explanation despite of repeated calls by the complainant then the complainant developed a suspicion.

On 13th June,
complainant visited .
the branch of Canara Bank, Kotwali Bazaar, Dharamshala and enquired about his bank account.
On enquiry, he has been apprised that on his documentary proof, account No.110103918500 has been opened in the Canara Bank branch on 20.02.2023.

When, the complainant obtained the statements of account, then, he was shocked to know that from 20.02.2023 to 30.04.2023, from his account,
transactions worth Rs.64,98,653.86/- have already been done.
When, he apprised the bank officials regarding the fact that he did not receive any message nor receive any mail then how these transactions can be made.
On this, the bank officials disclosed him that mobile No.6230086766 has been connected with the account and e-mail ID abdevilliers229 @ gmail.com has also been attached with the account.

When, the complainant persistently enquired from Sahil then, he has disclosed Neeshant Mehta vs The State Of H.P on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81671803/
2 that after opening the bank account, he used to supply the particulars to accused Sumit of Paprola,
who used to pay money in return to them.

10. Accused-Sahil r to was associated in the investigation and Notice under Section 41(A) of the Cr.P.C. was served upon him, but, he did not cooperate in the investigation and as such, he was arrested.
11.

Search of his vehicle No.DL-1CP-0918 was conducted and on search, R.C., Pan Card, ATM Cards,
Bank cheque book, account opening forms, SIM pouch and SIM cards were recovered, which were taken into possession.
On 16.06.2023, search of the house and shop of accused Sumit Arora was conducted and passbooks, ATM Cards, .
Cheque Books and laptops recovered from his house and shop were taken into possession.
12. On 17.06.2023, accused Sumit Arora was also arrested.
During interrogation, Sumit Arora disclosed that they used to hand over the record of ATM and bank accounts opened (applicant/accused).

13. On 17.06.2023, ASI Ramesh Kumar with police team was sent to Chandigarh in order to arrest applicant/accused.

sentences.text: On 18.06.2023, nine accused working on laptops and mobile phones in Flat No.42, TDI Sector 111 SAS Nagar of applicant/accused were found.
Laptops, mobile phones and other documents found in the flat were also taken into possession.

They were .
brought to Dharamshala.

During interrogation, they all told that they all were indulged in 'online gambling/Satta' and they are working in Mahadev company and Konark Book and applicant/accused Neeshant alias Shanki is the Head/owner of both the companies.
Numerous mobile phones, laptops and ATM cards have been recovered from their possession.

15. The investigation conducted so far reveals that applicant/accused Neeshant is the head of gang,
who has absconded and his arrest is necessary for further investigation of the case.

All nine accused detained at Chandigarh on 20.06.2023 were also arrested and produced before the Court and during investigation, they all again told that applicant/accused is their gang leader and they are indulged in 'online Satta/Gambling'.

16. The statements of accounts of some bank accounts have been received and as per statement of account No.082200JU00000192, which is in the name of Lovely Computer, transactions of a sum of .
Rs.1,92,93,487.7 have been made from 04.01.2022 to 17.06.2023, transactions of Rs.2,50,62,156.4 have been made through Account No.2578008700002728, which is opened in the name of the wife of accused Sumit as 'Kanika Repair Hub' and both these accounts are operated by the toapplicant/accused.
No.88148700007230 has been opened in the name of r Account Lovely Computer & Cyber City,

Sumit Arora and transactions of Rs.5,48,875/- have been made through this account from 01.02.2022 to 21.06.2023 and transactions of Rs.5,45,790/- have been made through Account No.50066338281 opened in the name of Lovely Computer, transactions of Rs.5,48,606/- have been made through Account No.50066376362, which is also opened in the name of Lovely Computer and daily transactions of thousands of rupees is found to be made through Account No.00000020138687655, which is opened in the name of accused Sumit Arora.
Similar transactions have been made through the accounts of Sahil and details of several accounts are yet to be .
obtained.

17. Thus, transactions in crores have been made through the aforesaid accounts and it appears that all transactions are false and applicant/accused is having information of the same as to from where the entire money was received.

19. It is further case of the police that in pursuance to the direction of this Court vide order dated 03.07.2023, applicant-Neeshant Mehta joined the investigation on 15th, 16th, 17th & 18th of July,
2023.
20.

Lastly, it is the case of the police that accused-Neeshant Mehta is the kingpin of the gang and other accused persons are working under him and in case, interim order is made absolute, the bail applicant may coerce the witnesses and also create obstacle in the arrest of the other accused persons.

On the basis of .
above facts, a prayer has been made to dismiss the bail application.
21. Heard.
Record perused.

22. The police, in the status report, has highlighted the fact that two criminal cases have already been registered against him particulars of which have been mentioned, in the application, as well as,
in the status report.
Admittedly, in those two cases, no conviction has been recorded by the competent court of law.
Merely, cases have been registered does not take away the presumption of innocence, which is still available to the accused-applicant.
The applicant is presumed to be innocent and dismissal of the present application amounts to remanding him to judicial custody or police custody.
The bail application cannot be rejected as to punish the accused prior to the trial as pre-trial punishment is prohibited under the law.

23. Considering the stand as taken by the police in the status report, the police is not able to make out a .
case for custodial interrogation.

So far as, the apprehensions, which have been expressed by the police in the status report are concerned, for those apprehensions, reasonable conditions, can be imposed in case, the bail application is allowed.

24. The chances of commencement conclusion of trial against the applicant, in near future, r and are not so bright and no useful purpose would be served by sending him to judicial custody.
25.

At the time of deciding the bail, the detailed discussions of the evidence, so collected by the I.O.,
during the investigation, should be avoided, as it would cause prejudice, to the case of the prosecution, as well as, to the case of the accused.
The accused is permanent resident of Kangra and as such, he will be readily available for the trial.
26. Considering all these facts, the interim order dated 03.07.2023 is made absolute.

Therefore, it is ordered that the applicant be released on bail, in the event of his arrest, in case FIR No.126 of 2023 Neeshant Mehta vs The State Of H.P on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81671803/
5 dated .
15.06.2023
registered
under Section 420, 468, 120-B read with Section 34 of the Indian & 66C &
66D of Information & Technology Act, 2000

with Police Station Dharamshala, District Kangra, H.P.
on his furnishing personal bond, to the tune of Rs.1,00,000/-, with one surety of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer.

Any of the observations, made herein above, shall not be taken, as an expression of opinion, on the merits of the case, as these observations are confined, only to the disposal of the present bail application 28.

The applicant is directed to move regular bail application, when report under Section 173(2)
Cr.P.C will be filed in the Competent Court of Law.
29 . It is made clear that the respondent-State is at liberty to move an appropriate application, in case, any of the bail conditions, is found violated by the applicant.

(Virender Singh) Judge July 18, 2023 (Pathania)
